( 3 ) Alfred Marshall : In his book,

'Principles
of Economics' published in 1890. Alfred
Marshall defines, 'Economics is the study of
mankind in the ordinary business of life.·
According to him economics keeps human
well-being at the centre of human activity
and explains how well-being is attained
from material consumption.

In Indian thought the four purposes of human
being are 'dharma', 'arth', 'kama' and 'moksha'.
The activities of life done for 'arth' are the
subject matter of economics.
Kautilya in his book 'Arthshashtra' discussed
economics as economic activity undertaken by
a state or society for creating arth.
In Indian thought intention of economic activities do not remain only for creating arth,
but are done considering human welfare. So
Kautilya called 'Economics' as 'Ethics·.
